ags-ptr-leg2-36-8.summary: Five days after Tordesillas was retaken from the Comuneros, Lope Hurtado de Mendoza, Charles V’s confidant with the governors of Castile, wrote two letters on the same day. One, in plain text, tells of the sack of the town and the capture of the Junta’s procurators; Danvila printed it in the late nineteenth century. The other, entirely in cipher, says what could not be written openly: the Admiral hesitates to govern, the Marquis of Denia is hated, the army is “very badly commanded”, and the see of Jaén and every vacancy should be held back to keep loyalties. An archivist’s slip in the bundle said the key was to be found in a letter of 23 September; it was not. We rebuilt it from the letter itself.
ags-ptr-leg2-36-8.en: The ·fre· wants a settlement with the men of the Junta at any price; he says he does so because of the poor means {there are} of maintaining the troops here. He had the Queen say, before the ·y· and many knights, that she ordered all the Junta’s troops to disperse, and had this recorded as testimony to summon don Pedro Girón ·y· the cities with it. The Count of Benavente, the Marquis of Astorga, the Count of Miranda and the Grand Commander were not there; on learning it, ·ym· at once set about remedying it. So they went to the ·fre·, and the testimony was torn up ‹…›, not by his vote: he stood in between. And even so, he said that he held the Queen to be of sound mind, and ‹…› a thousand times a day, so that {I fear} he may one day do something about the agreements that would be very harmful.

system: homophonic letter substitution (≈ 35 signs: barred o = t, cross = s, 9 = a, ſ = g, ⊤ = z…), words separated, a few dotted sigla for persons (·fre·, ·lis·, ·los·, ·lus·, ·ym·); the last words of the letter in mixed plain text
